mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS (as a continuous variable) and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 235, it signals accelerating inflation, prompting central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 235, or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL (as a binary indicator) and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and employment (PAYEMS) exceeds 136500, it indicates a tight labor market with strong job growth, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns through elevated consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE < 5% AND PAYEMS > 136500, or the interaction term (UNRATE * PAYEMS) has a negative coefficient in a regression of 20-day returns on UNRATE and PAYEMS with interaction, and the coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 exhibits negative 20-day forward returns due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the rank correlation between the regime indicator (FEDFUNDS>4.5%) and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeds 100, it signals robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns through sustained corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO > 100, or the rank correlation between INDPRO (as a continuous variable) and 60-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 850, it indicates a weakening housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to reduced consumer confidence and economic slowdown fears.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST < 850, or the rank correlation between HOUST (as a binary indicator) and 5-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 900 and residential fixed investment (RSAFS) exceeds 426000, it signals a strong housing market and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST > 900 AND RSAFS > 426000, or the interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) has a negative coefficient in a regression of 20-day returns on HOUST and RSAFS with interaction, and the coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 890, it indicates a strengthening housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns through sustained consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST > 890, or the rank correlation between HOUST (as a continuous variable) and 60-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.
